mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕劳动与工作展开，涵盖工作的意义（Reading）、为职业生涯做准备（Extended reading）、量入为出·珍惜劳动（Grammar and usage）和从校园到职场·资历与技能（Integrated skills）四个板块——劳动价值与职业规划是高考应用文'演讲/申请'类的常见立意，也是雅思工作与教育类议论文的核心命题。

subTopics.title: 工作的意义
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：我们工作不只是因为需要 the salary that enables us to be financially independent——our work, when done well, will not only help us make a living but also help make a life。

prompts.task: 你校英语社团以 "Why We Work" 为题举办演讲活动。请你写一篇发言稿，谈谈你对工作意义的理解，内容包括：1. 常见看法；2. 你的观点；3. 简短总结。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Good afternoon, everyone. When we ask why people work, the first answer is usually money.

It is certainly true that most of us join the labour force once our studies are completed, and that we need a salary to be financially independent. But is that all? I don't think so. Our work, when done well, does not only help us make a living; it also helps us make a life. Through our labour we gain confidence, earn respect, and feel that we matter to others.

So as we prepare for our future careers, let us look beyond the pay check. A job feeds the body, but meaningful work feeds the soul. Choose work you can be proud of. Thank you!
vocabHints: the first answer is usually money

prompts.task: Some people work mainly to earn money, while others believe that work should also give life meaning and a sense of purpose. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
People go to work for very different reasons. For some, a job is simply a way to earn a living; for others, work should also provide meaning and a sense of purpose. Having considered both, I believe that while income is a necessary motive, work that also brings purpose enriches life in ways money alone cannot.

Those who work mainly for money have practical sense on their side. A salary pays for housing, food and security, and allows people to support their families and enjoy life outside the office; not everyone can find a dream career, and there is dignity in working hard simply to provide. For many, a job is valued precisely because it funds what they truly care about elsewhere.

Yet treating work as nothing more than a pay cheque overlooks how much of life it occupies. People spend most of their waking hours working, and a job that offers only money but no interest, respect or growth often leads to boredom and quiet unhappiness. Work done well builds confidence and identity; it lets people feel useful and connected to something beyond themselves. This is why many accept lower pay for jobs they find meaningful, and why sudden retirement can leave even the wealthy feeling lost.

In my view, the ideal is to satisfy both needs. A job must first pay enough to live on, but wherever possible people should also seek work that engages them, because purpose turns mere employment into a source of lasting satisfaction.

In conclusion, money is an essential reason to work, but meaning is what makes work worth doing.

subTopics.title: 量入为出·珍惜劳动
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：on a tight budget、within budget、economize、weigh the benefits against the cost——劳动来之不易，学会规划花销，才对得起每一分辛苦钱。

prompts.task: 针对部分同学花钱大手大脚的现象，请你以学生会名义用英文写一份倡议书，倡导理性消费，内容包括：1. 现象与看法；2. 两三条建议；3. 号召。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear fellow students,

Lately some of us spend money as fast as we get it, forgetting how hard our parents work to earn it. The Student Union hopes we can all learn to live within our means.

Here are a few tips. First, make a simple monthly plan and try to stay within your budget. Second, before every purchase, weigh whether you truly need it against how much it costs. Third, learn to economise — a saved yuan is a earned yuan. None of this means being stingy; it means respecting the labour behind every note in our pockets.

Money managed wisely gives us freedom, not limits. Let's spend thoughtfully, and value what we have.

The Student Union
vocabHints: spend money as fast as we get it
weigh whether you truly need it

prompts.task: Some people believe that schools should teach children how to manage money and personal finance. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Many young people leave school able to solve equations yet unable to budget, and some argue that money management should be a formal part of the curriculum. I strongly agree, because financial skills are essential to adult life and are too often left untaught.

The main reason is sheer usefulness. Almost every adult must earn, spend, save and borrow, and mistakes in these areas cause real suffering — crippling debt, ruined credit, an old age without savings. Yet these skills are rarely learned at home, especially by children whose parents struggle with money themselves. A school course covering budgeting, the dangers of debt, basic saving and how interest works would give every student, rich or poor, the tools to avoid predictable disasters. Unlike much of what is memorised for exams, this knowledge is used for life.

There are, of course, objections. The timetable is already crowded, and some argue that finance is better taught by families. But families often lack the knowledge to pass on, which is exactly why schools should ensure no child is left ignorant; and financial education need not replace core subjects, since it can be woven into mathematics or citizenship lessons.

Taught well — practically, with real examples rather than dry theory — such lessons could prevent a lifetime of costly errors and help young people value the labour their money represents.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that schools should teach personal finance. Few subjects are more directly useful, and equipping the young to manage money wisely is among the most valuable preparations a school can offer for real life.

subTopics.title: 从校园到职场·资历与技能
subTopics.desc: 综合技能板块核心词块：qualifications、be qualified for、the proportion of graduates——一纸文凭是敲门砖，真正让你站稳脚跟的，是把资历变成能力。

prompts.task: 你校邀请一位职场前辈就'如何从校园走向职场'做分享。请你用英文写一篇报道，内容包括：1. 分享的主要建议；2. 你的收获。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Last Friday, our school invited Ms Chen, a company manager, to share how students can move from campus to the workplace.

Her advice was down to earth. Qualifications matter, she said, but they only get you an interview; whether you are truly qualified for a job depends on skills you must keep building — communication, teamwork and a willingness to learn. She noted that only a small proportion of graduates fail because of poor grades; far more struggle because they cannot apply what they know.

What I took away was simple but powerful: a diploma opens the door, but ability keeps you in the room. From now on, I will practise real skills, not just chase marks. It was a lesson no exam could teach.
vocabHints: move from campus to the workplace
her advice was down to earth
qualifications only get you an interview

prompts.task: Some people believe that practical work experience is more valuable than academic qualifications. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
In the debate over what best prepares people for their careers, some claim that hands-on work experience beats any diploma. I partly agree: experience is indispensable and often undervalued, but for most fields it complements formal qualifications rather than replacing them.

Experience has clear advantages. It teaches what classrooms cannot — how a real workplace functions, how to deal with colleagues and customers, how to solve messy problems that have no textbook answer. Employers value it precisely because it proves a person can apply knowledge, not merely recite it, and many highly successful people built careers on practical skill rather than degrees. In creative and technical trades especially, a strong portfolio can outweigh any certificate.

Nevertheless, dismissing qualifications goes too far. Many professions — medicine, engineering, law — require a deep theoretical foundation that only structured study provides, and no amount of on-the-job trial and error can safely substitute for it. Qualifications also open doors: they signal to employers that a candidate has the knowledge and discipline to be trained further, and without them many jobs are simply closed. For most people, the two work together — study supplies the principles, experience turns them into competence.

My own view is that neither alone is enough. The ideal path combines solid qualifications with real experience, whether through internships, part-time work or projects, so that graduates leave not only knowing but able to do.

In conclusion, while practical experience is enormously valuable and sometimes decisive, it is usually most powerful alongside academic qualifications, not instead of them. The strongest candidates are those who possess both.

subTopics.title: 为职业生涯做准备
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：面对求职，你需要 apply for a job、gain some prior knowledge、prioritize your tasks 并 build up a clear profile——机会往往留给有准备的人。

prompts.task: 你想申请一家英文杂志社的暑期实习。请你用英文写一封申请信，内容包括：1. 写信目的；2. 你的优势与准备；3. 表达期待。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the summer internship at your magazine advertised on your website.

As a Senior 2 student with a strong interest in writing, I have prepared carefully for this opportunity. I have gained some prior knowledge of editing by running our school English newspaper, where I learned to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines. I would be glad to share a short profile of my work if that would help.

Although the odds may be against a student with little formal experience, I am a fast learner and eager to contribute. I would welcome the chance of an interview at your convenience. Thank you for considering my application.

Yours faithfully,
Li Hua
vocabHints: a short profile of my work

prompts.task: Some people think that the main purpose of schools is to prepare students for the world of work, while others believe schools should provide a broader education. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Educators disagree about what schools are chiefly for. Some argue their central task is to prepare young people for employment; others believe education should develop the whole person, not merely a future worker. In my opinion schools must do both, but a broad education should remain the foundation on which job-related skills are built.

The argument for work preparation is practical. Young people must eventually earn a living, and schools that ignore this leave graduates unready for real life. Teaching relevant skills — from digital literacy to teamwork and financial sense — improves employment prospects and strengthens the economy, and few would deny that these matter greatly to students and society alike.

Yet reducing school to job training is short-sighted. The specific skills a job needs change rapidly, and today's students may one day do jobs that do not yet exist. What lasts is the broader capacity that education builds: the ability to think critically, to learn new things, to understand history, science and other cultures, and to become a thoughtful citizen and a rounded human being. A narrow, purely vocational schooling produces workers who cannot adapt and citizens who cannot reflect.

The wisest approach, then, blends the two. Schools should equip students with practical, employable skills while also cultivating curiosity, character and the ability to keep learning — for it is broad education that allows people to master new work throughout their lives.

In conclusion, while preparing students for work is a legitimate goal, it should not crowd out the wider purpose of education. The best schools prepare young people not just for a first job, but for a whole life.
